provider.name: Chart Hands
provider.description: Analyze CSV data and build, check and read Plotly charts

descriptor.instructions: For CSV exploration use eda_profile for schema and missingness, then eda_analyze: summary for one overall total or average of a column (with filter for a period), aggregate for one value per group (shares, top groups, change between periods), histogram, Pearson correlation, rows; quote its computed numbers instead of doing arithmetic yourself. Use filter to select rows and rows to inspect paginated cells. Column meanings and units are not in the CSV: before reading values as amounts or ratios, check the notes the host lists as mentioning the file. Interpret excluded rows and undefined correlations. Choose charts from results; these tools never edit data. Tools for Plotly charts in Obsidian notes (Chart Hands). A chart is a plotly fenced block of YAML or JSON with only data (list of traces), layout, config and fit as top-level keys. Quote colours ("#2563EB") and date-like strings; use no functions or variables. Write titles as objects: title: {text: "..."}. Choose charts for the question (get_chart_guide basics): trend, comparison, share, distribution, relationship, matrix, hierarchy, flow, stages, profile or KPI. Use Plotly's advanced types (heatmap, box, violin, treemap, sunburst, sankey, waterfall, funnel, candlestick, polar, contour, 3D, maps, subplots, buttons) when the data has that shape. Call get_chart_guide when unsure (topics: basics, style, examples, statistical, hierarchy, timeseries, scientific, maps, layout, dataviewjs, errors). For values from a vault CSV, use build_chart with source; never copy the numbers by hand. Write a block yourself only for types build_chart lacks. Run check_chart on the block content (without the fence lines) before writing it into a note, and fix every problem it reports. Insert the block with the host's note-editing tools: none of these tools edits a note or draws a chart. read_charts lists and checks the plotly blocks already in a note. The check verifies the definition against Plotly's rules, not its appearance on screen.

tools.name: eda_profile
tools.title: Profile a CSV dataset
tools.description: Read a vault CSV and infer columns, missing rates, distinct counts, frequent values and numeric descriptive statistics. Blank or whitespace-only cells are missing; a numeric column needs every nonblank value to be a number in one unit (1,234, 12%, ₩5, △5 negative; a unitless 0 takes the column unit). Returns ten columns per page. CSV must have unique headers and at most 100000 rows, 100 columns and 5 MiB. Does not modify files or load Plotly.

path.description: Vault-relative CSV path, or a Markdown note (.md); its pipe table is read (table picks which, 1-based, default 1).

table.description: Markdown notes only: which pipe table to read, 1-based; default 1.

from.description: 1-based first column of this page; defaults to 1. When more columns remain, the result gives nextFrom: call again with from set to it.

tools.name: eda_analyze
tools.title: Analyze a CSV dataset
tools.description: filter ANDs up to four conditions: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, prefix, contains. Numbers compare numerically, else as strings. Period: {"column":"연월","op":"gte","value":"2025-01"} plus lte. summary gives count, sum, mean, min, max for each of 1–8 numeric columns over matching rows; use it for one overall total or average, e.g. a year's monthly average with a filter. With 2–8 columns it also gives each column's share of their combined sum. histogram takes one column, correlation two. aggregate groups columns[0], reduces columns[1]: one value per group by sum, mean, count, min, max or median; count may omit the value column. For mean, min, max or median it also returns overall, the same function over all matching rows. Sort desc, asc, label or original; label and original give change from the previous group. Groups have shares and chart data. rows: cells and row numbers, paged by limit and offset. 1,234, 12%, ₩5 and △5 (negative) are numbers; mixed units are refused.

path.description: Vault-relative CSV path, or a Markdown note (.md); its pipe table is read (table picks which, 1-based, default 1).

table.description: Markdown notes only: which pipe table to read, 1-based; default 1.

filter.description: Up to four conditions combined with AND before analysis.

value.description: Value to compare against the cell.

bins.description: Histogram bin count, default 10; intervals are left-closed, right-open except the last.

function.description: aggregate only. Default sum with a value column, count without. summary ignores it and returns every statistic.

sort.description: aggregate: desc (default), asc, label, original; rows: asc (default) or desc with sort_by.

sort_by.description: rows only. Sort by this CSV column before pagination.

limit.description: aggregate: default 60, maximum 100 groups (larger values are rejected). rows: default 50; requests above 100 are capped at 100 with limitApplied and offset guidance.

tools.name: check_chart
tools.title: Check a Plotly chart
tools.description: Check the content of a plotly code block (YAML or JSON): that it parses, that the top-level keys are only data, layout, config and fit, that trace and layout attributes and values suit Plotly, and common mistakes such as unquoted colours. Returns a list of problems. Call it before writing a chart block into a note. Does not change any note.

source.description: The content that goes inside a plotly code block, without the fence lines: YAML with data: and layout: each starting its own line (use \n in this string), or one JSON object such as {"data":[…],"layout":{…}}. Do not join keys with commas on one line.

tools.name: read_charts
tools.title: Read the Plotly charts in a note
tools.description: Find the plotly code blocks in a note and return, for each chart, its line range, trace types and point counts, title, and the problems found by the check. Returns at most 20 charts per call and gives the next from value when there are more. Charts drawn with dataviewjs are counted but not checked.

path.description: Vault-relative path of a Markdown note.

from.description: Start reading at this chart number. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: get_chart_guide
tools.title: Plotly chart writing guide
tools.description: Return guidance for writing Plotly chart blocks for Chart Hands. Topics: basics (block format, YAML rules, which chart type fits which question, workflow), style (polished look: palette, margins, labels, annotations), examples (line, bar and pie blocks), statistical (histogram, box, violin, correlation heatmap, density, splom, error bars), hierarchy (treemap, sunburst, icicle, sankey, waterfall, funnel, parcats), timeseries (date axes, range slider and buttons, candlestick, event shading, KPI indicator and gauge), scientific (contour, 3D surface, polar, wind rose, ternary, parallel coordinates, table), maps (choropleth, scattergeo, tile maps), layout (subplots, secondary axis, rich hover, reference lines, buttons, sliders), dataviewjs (dynamic charts), errors (fixing charts that do not render). Read basics before writing a chart by hand.

tools.name: build_chart
tools.title: Build a Plotly chart block
tools.description: CSV의 값을 그릴 때는 값을 옮겨 적지 말고 source와 series[].column을 준다. Build a plotly block with basic checks; use check_chart for full validation. source:{path,labels?,x?,filter?,sort?,limit?} reads CSV rows (1–200 after filtering and limit). For a top-N chart pass source.sort and source.limit instead of sorting with eda_analyze and copying the values. source.labels names the category column; scatter/bubble require source.x; bubble also requires series[].sizeColumn. Do not combine source with labels or series values/x/size. Blank numeric cells become gaps; non-numeric columns are rejected. Without source, supply series[].values; per-label types need labels, scatter/bubble need x (bubble also size), histogram/box/violin use observations, indicator uses [value,reference?]. combo uses kind; secondary uses the right axis. treemap/sunburst need parents. Returns block and compatible compact staticBlock for HWPX. Insert with host note-editing tools; no file is changed.

path.description: Vault-relative CSV path, or a Markdown note (.md); its pipe table is read (table picks which, 1-based, default 1).

table.description: Markdown notes only: which pipe table to read, 1-based; default 1.

labels.description: CSV category column; required for per-label chart types.

x.description: Numeric CSV x column; required for scatter and bubble.

filter.description: Same AND conditions as eda_analyze; applied before charting, without pagination.

limit.description: Maximum rows after filtering and sorting.

labels.description: Category names (x axis; y axis for barh and funnel stages), slice or node names (pie, donut, treemap, sunburst), heatmap columns or radar axes. Not used by scatter, bubble, histogram, box, violin or indicator.

parents.description: treemap and sunburst: the parent label of each label, "" for a top-level item.

measure.description: waterfall: per label, relative (a change, the default), total (running total; its value is ignored) or absolute (sets the level).

column.description: Numeric CSV column; required with source. Without source provide values instead.

sizeColumn.description: Numeric CSV size column; required for bubble with source.

name.description: Series name, shown in the legend.

values.description: One number per label (per x for scatter and bubble), or raw observations for histogram, box and violin.

x.description: scatter and bubble: the x value of each point.

size.description: bubble: the size measure of each point (drawn as area).

text.description: scatter and bubble: a hover label for each point.

kind.description: combo: how to draw this series. Defaults to bar for the first series and line for the others.

secondary.description: line, area, bar, combo: draw this series against a right-hand y axis (a different unit).

x_title.description: Horizontal axis title. Include the unit.

y_title.description: Vertical axis title. Include the unit.

y2_title.description: Right-hand axis title, for series with secondary. Include the unit.

stacked.description: Stack several bar, area or histogram series instead of grouping or overlaying them.

bins.description: histogram: the maximum number of bins.

range_slider.description: line, area, bar, combo, scatter, bubble: add a range slider under the x axis for long series.

style.description: clean (default) applies the palette and tidy layout; plain adds nothing beyond the data.

Chart Hands renders a fenced code block whose language is "plotly". The block content is YAML (or JSON) with these top-level keys only: data, layout, config, fit. Any other key stops the chart from drawing.

- data: list of Plotly traces. Give every trace a "type" and its value arrays.
- layout: title, axis titles, legend, barmode, margins and other static display settings.
- config: static UI settings such as responsive: true and displaylogo: false.
- fit: off, shrink or fill. Controls width fitting for this chart. Leave it out unless asked.

YAML rules that matter:
- Quote every colour: color: "#2563EB". An unquoted # starts a YAML comment and the value becomes null.
- Quote date-like strings ("2026-01-01") so they stay strings.
- Quote strings that contain a colon.
- Write titles as objects: title: {text: "Monthly sales"}, also for axes (xaxis: {title: {text: "Month"}}) and colour bars. This Plotly version does not show a title given as a plain string.
- Quote single letters used as values, such as overlaying: "y", so no YAML parser reads them as booleans.
- Write arrays as YAML lists or flow lists ([1, 2, 3]). Convert JSON examples into YAML indentation instead of pasting them.
- Use only static values: no JavaScript functions, callbacks, variables, template expressions or undefined.

Choosing a chart type. Pick by the question the chart answers, not by habit; [name] is the build_chart type, (topic) is the get_chart_guide topic with a hand-written example.
- Trend over time: line [line]. Volume or part-to-whole over time: stacked area [area]. Long daily or price series: add range_slider, or candlestick/ohlc (timeseries).
- Compare categories: bar [bar]; long labels or more than about 8 items: horizontal bar [barh], sorted by value. Two measures with different units: bars plus a line on a secondary y axis [combo].
- Share of a whole: pie or donut [pie, donut], only with up to 6 parts; otherwise a sorted bar. Nested shares: treemap or sunburst [treemap, sunburst], icicle (hierarchy).
- How a total builds up from gains and losses: waterfall [waterfall]. Drop-off through stages: funnel [funnel]. Flows between groups or stages: sankey (hierarchy).
- Distribution of raw values: histogram [histogram]. Compare distributions across groups: box or violin [box, violin]. Two-variable density: histogram2dcontour (statistical).
- Relationship between two measures: scatter [scatter]; a third measure as point size: bubble [bubble]; many variables at once: splom or parcoords (statistical, scientific). Uncertainty: error bars or a confidence band (statistical).
- Values on a grid such as weekday by hour, or a correlation matrix: heatmap [heatmap]. A function of two variables: contour or surface (scientific).
- Profile of items across several criteria: radar [radar]. Direction and magnitude: barpolar wind rose (scientific). Three parts that sum to a constant: scatterternary (scientific).
- One headline number with its change: indicator [indicator]; a gauge or a KPI row (timeseries, layout).
- Places: scattergeo or choropleth, tile maps with scattermap (maps).
- Several panels, a secondary axis, buttons, sliders, reference lines or rich hover text: (layout).

Prefer the simplest chart that answers the question. Use an advanced type when the data really has that shape (hierarchy, flow, distribution, matrix), not for decoration, and say in one line why you chose it.

Keep the user's units and order. If a unit is unclear, do not convert it; show the original unit in an axis title.

Workflow: write the block, call check_chart with the block content (without the fence lines), fix every problem it reports, then insert the block into the note with the host's note-editing tools. These tools never change notes themselves. build_chart produces a checked block for every [name] type above; write the other types by hand from the topic examples.

Other topics: style, examples, statistical, hierarchy, timeseries, scientific, maps, layout, dataviewjs, errors.

Apply this only when the user asks for a polished, clean or report-ready look. These are structure hints, not a finished chart: rewrite the real data, units, titles, hover text and annotations every time.

Palette (always quoted in YAML): primary "#2563EB", highlight "#C2410C", neutral "#64748B", grid "#E2E8F0", text "#334155", title "#0F172A", series 2 "#0F766E", series 3 "#7C3AED". Do not tell series apart by colour alone: also vary the line dash, marker symbol or labels.

layout:
  margin: {l: 50, r: 30, t: 90, b: 50, autoexpand: true}
  xaxis: {automargin: true, showgrid: false, showline: false, zeroline: false}
  yaxis: {automargin: true, showgrid: true, gridcolor: "#E2E8F0", griddash: "dot", showline: false, zeroline: false}
config:
  responsive: true
  displaylogo: false

Notes:
- Automatic margins belong on axes and titles (automargin) and in margin.autoexpand, not at the top level of layout.
- Skip a fixed height and a horizontal legend for long titles or narrow panes.
- hovermode "x unified" suits series that share an x axis.
- Bar value labels: texttemplate "%{y:,.12~g}" for vertical bars, "%{x:,.12~g}" for horizontal bars preserves meaningful decimals. Match the format and units to the data; with textposition "outside" and cliponaxis false, check margins and negative values.
- Annotations: use only when needed (1 to 3), set xref and yref, and base causes or events on the user's material, never on the data alone.
- Plotly.js draws a white background and does not inherit the Obsidian theme. State a white background only for report or print requests; for a dark look set explicit colours for paper_bgcolor, plot_bgcolor, font and grid.
- When editing an existing chart, keep its data, layout, config, colours, axis ranges and uirevision and merge only the style properties you need.

Other topics: basics, examples, statistical, hierarchy, timeseries, scientific, maps, layout, dataviewjs, errors.

Line chart:
```plotly
data:
  - x: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr"]
    y: [120, 150, 135, 180]
    type: scatter
    mode: lines+markers
    name: "Sales"
    line:
      color: "#2563EB"
layout:
  title:
    text: "Monthly sales"
  xaxis:
    title:
      text: "Month"
  yaxis:
    title:
      text: "Sales (10k KRW)"
config:
  responsive: true
```

Bar chart:
```plotly
data:
  - x: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]
    y: [120, 200, 150, 180]
    type: bar
    name: "Result"
layout:
  title:
    text: "Quarterly results"
  barmode: group
  yaxis:
    title:
      text: "Amount (10k KRW)"
```

Pie chart:
```plotly
data:
  - type: pie
    labels: ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
    values: [40, 25, 20, 15]
layout:
  title:
    text: "Share by item"
```

Other topics: basics, style, statistical, hierarchy, timeseries, scientific, maps, layout, dataviewjs, errors.

Distributions, uncertainty and relationships. Replace the sample numbers with the user's data.

Overlaid histograms (raw values, Plotly does the binning; barmode overlay plus opacity keeps both visible; histnorm "percent" compares groups of different size):
```plotly
data:
  - {type: histogram, x: [52, 61, 58, 70, 66, 59, 73, 64, 68, 55], name: "Class A", nbinsx: 8, opacity: 0.6, marker: {color: "#2563EB"}}
  - {type: histogram, x: [48, 57, 62, 51, 60, 54, 49, 63, 58, 50], name: "Class B", nbinsx: 8, opacity: 0.6, marker: {color: "#C2410C"}}
layout:
  title: {text: "Score distribution"}
  barmode: overlay
  xaxis: {title: {text: "Score"}}
  yaxis: {title: {text: "Students"}}
```

Box or violin by group: one trace per series; for groups inside each series give x as a category per point and set layout.boxmode (violinmode) to group. boxpoints "all" with jitter 0.3 shows every point when there are few. Violin: box: {visible: true}, meanline: {visible: true}, side "positive" for half violins.
```plotly
data:
  - {type: box, name: "Plant 1", y: [4.1, 4.5, 3.9, 5.2, 4.8, 6.9], boxmean: sd, boxpoints: all, jitter: 0.3}
  - {type: violin, name: "Plant 2", y: [5.0, 5.4, 4.7, 5.9, 5.1, 5.6], box: {visible: true}, meanline: {visible: true}}
layout:
  title: {text: "Cycle time by plant"}
  yaxis: {title: {text: "Minutes"}}
  showlegend: false
```

Correlation matrix heatmap: fixed zmin -1, zmax 1 and a diverging scale centred on 0 (reversescale puts positive values in blue); texttemplate prints the value in each cell; autorange reversed keeps the first row on top.
```plotly
data:
  - type: heatmap
    x: ["Price", "Ads", "Visits", "Sales"]
    y: ["Price", "Ads", "Visits", "Sales"]
    z: [[1, -0.2, -0.4, -0.5], [-0.2, 1, 0.7, 0.6], [-0.4, 0.7, 1, 0.8], [-0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1]]
    zmin: -1
    zmax: 1
    colorscale: RdBu
    reversescale: true
    texttemplate: "%{z:.2f}"
    xgap: 2
    ygap: 2
layout:
  title: {text: "Correlation"}
  yaxis: {autorange: reversed}
```

Density of many points: histogram2dcontour (or histogram2d) with x and y arrays, ncontours 15, colorscale Blues, optionally under a scatter trace with small translucent markers.

Scatter matrix (splom) for 3 to 6 numeric variables:
```plotly
data:
  - type: splom
    dimensions:
      - {label: "Height (cm)", values: [160, 172, 181, 168, 175]}
      - {label: "Weight (kg)", values: [55, 70, 82, 63, 74]}
      - {label: "Age", values: [23, 35, 41, 29, 38]}
    text: ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]
    marker: {size: 7, color: "#2563EB", line: {color: "#FFFFFF", width: 0.5}}
    diagonal: {visible: false}
    showupperhalf: false
layout:
  title: {text: "Body measures"}
```

Uncertainty:
- Error bars: error_y: {type: data, array: [0.4, 0.3, 0.5], visible: true}; asymmetric with symmetric: false and arrayminus. error_x works the same way.
- Confidence band: an upper trace with line width 0, then a lower trace with fill tonexty and fillcolor "rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.15)", then the mean line. Set showlegend: false on the band traces.

Trend lines and moving averages: Plotly does not fit them. Compute the fitted or averaged values from the user's data yourself, add them as an extra line trace (dash "dash") and say how they were computed.

Hierarchies, flows and step-by-step totals.

Treemap, sunburst and icicle take the same data: labels (unique; use ids when two nodes share a name), parents ("" for a top-level node) and values. branchvalues "total" means a parent's value is the sum of its children; it draws nothing when a parent is smaller than its children, so leave branchvalues out (remainder: a parent's value is added to its children) unless the parent values are exact sums. Use maxdepth 2 for deep trees, and textinfo "label+value+percent parent". Change type to sunburst or icicle without changing the data; icicle takes tiling: {orientation: v} for a top-down layout.
```plotly
data:
  - type: treemap
    labels: ["Total", "Hardware", "Software", "Services", "Laptops", "Phones", "Licences", "Cloud"]
    parents: ["", "Total", "Total", "Total", "Hardware", "Hardware", "Software", "Software"]
    values: [100, 45, 35, 20, 25, 20, 15, 20]
    branchvalues: total
    textinfo: "label+value+percent parent"
    marker: {line: {color: "#FFFFFF", width: 2}}
layout:
  title: {text: "Revenue by segment (100M KRW)"}
  margin: {l: 10, r: 10, t: 60, b: 10}
```

Sankey for flows between groups or stages: node.label lists every node once; link.source and link.target are 0-based indexes into node.label; link.value is the size of each flow. All three link arrays must have the same length. Give node colours and translucent link colours; arrangement snap lets the user drag nodes.
```plotly
data:
  - type: sankey
    arrangement: snap
    node:
      label: ["Visitors", "Sign-up", "Bounce", "Paid", "Free"]
      color: ["#64748B", "#2563EB", "#C2410C", "#0F766E", "#7C3AED"]
      pad: 18
      thickness: 16
    link:
      source: [0, 0, 1, 1]
      target: [1, 2, 3, 4]
      value: [620, 380, 140, 480]
      color: ["rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.3)", "rgba(194, 65, 12, 0.3)", "rgba(15, 118, 110, 0.3)", "rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.3)"]
layout:
  title: {text: "Visitor flow"}
```

Waterfall for how a starting value becomes an ending value: measure lists relative (a change), total (draws the running total; its y is ignored, use 0) or absolute (resets the level) for each x.
```plotly
data:
  - type: waterfall
    x: ["Revenue", "Cost of sales", "Gross profit", "Opex", "Tax", "Net profit"]
    measure: [absolute, relative, total, relative, relative, total]
    y: [500, -210, 0, -150, -35, 0]
    texttemplate: "%{delta:,.0f}"
    textposition: outside
    increasing: {marker: {color: "#0F766E"}}
    decreasing: {marker: {color: "#C2410C"}}
    totals: {marker: {color: "#2563EB"}}
    connector: {line: {color: "#64748B", dash: dot}}
layout:
  title: {text: "Profit bridge (M KRW)"}
  showlegend: false
```

Funnel for drop-off through ordered stages: y holds the stages top to bottom, x the counts; textinfo "value+percent initial" (or "percent previous"). Several funnel traces with layout.funnelmode group compare segments side by side. funnelarea draws a proportional funnel from labels and values, like a pie.

Parallel categories (parcats) shows how records split across several categorical dimensions: dimensions: [{label: "Plan", values: [...]}, {label: "Region", values: [...]}], one value per record in every dimension; colour by a number with line: {color: [...], colorscale: Blues}.

Prefer a sorted bar chart when there is only one level, and a sankey only when the flows really connect stages.

Maps need an internet connection: geo traces download country outlines and tile maps download map tiles. Say so when you add one, and offer a bar chart of the same values for offline use.

Choropleth or bubble map of countries (geo): locations are ISO-3 codes with locationmode ISO-3.
```plotly
data:
  - type: choropleth
    locationmode: ISO-3
    locations: ["KOR", "JPN", "USA", "DEU", "FRA"]
    z: [52, 41, 77, 63, 58]
    text: ["Korea", "Japan", "United States", "Germany", "France"]
    colorscale: Blues
    colorbar: {title: {text: "Index"}}
    marker: {line: {color: "#FFFFFF", width: 0.5}}
layout:
  title: {text: "Index by country"}
  geo: {projection: {type: "natural earth"}, showframe: false, showcoastlines: false, showland: true, landcolor: "#F1F5F9"}
```
scattergeo takes lat and lon (or locations) and marker.size for bubbles; layout.geo.scope (asia, europe, usa, ...) zooms to a region, and fitbounds locations zooms to the data.

Tile maps (MapLibre): scattermap, densitymap and choroplethmap with layout.map. The free styles open-street-map, carto-positron and carto-darkmatter need no token.
```plotly
data:
  - type: scattermap
    lat: [37.5665, 35.1796, 35.8714]
    lon: [126.978, 129.0756, 128.6014]
    text: ["Seoul", "Busan", "Daegu"]
    mode: "markers+text"
    textposition: "top right"
    marker: {size: [18, 12, 10], color: "#2563EB"}
layout:
  title: {text: "Offices"}
  map: {style: carto-positron, center: {lat: 36.3, lon: 127.8}, zoom: 5.5}
  margin: {l: 0, r: 0, t: 50, b: 0}
```
choroplethmap needs geojson: a URL string to a GeoJSON file, with featureidkey matching locations. The mapbox traces (scattermapbox, choroplethmapbox, densitymapbox) and layout.mapbox no longer exist in this Plotly version; use the map ones.

- The block shows as plain code: the Chart Hands plugin is disabled, or the code fence language is not exactly "plotly".
- "Couldn't render plot": check that the top-level keys are only data, layout, config and fit, and that YAML indentation, quotes and list syntax are valid. Run check_chart on the block content.
- A colour is ignored or null: it was written without quotes. Write color: "#2563EB".
- A date axis shows odd values: quote the date strings.
- Nothing is drawn and no error is shown: the code fence may be unclosed; read_charts reports blocks without a closing fence.
- The chart is clipped in PDF export: the plugin setting "Fit the page width when exporting to PDF" can be turned on.
- A treemap, sunburst or icicle is empty: every parent must be one of the labels (or ""), labels must be unique (or use ids), and with branchvalues total a parent must not be smaller than the sum of its children. Remove branchvalues to fall back to remainder.
- A sankey shows no links: link.source and link.target are 0-based indexes into node.label, and source, target and value need the same length.
- A heatmap, contour or surface is blank: z must be a list of rows (a list of lists), with one entry per x in each row.
- A map stays empty: maps need an internet connection; mapbox trace types do not exist in this Plotly version (use scattermap, choroplethmap, densitymap with layout.map).
- A 3D or WebGL chart is blank: WebGL may be unavailable, or the note has too many WebGL charts.
- check_chart reports a title "must be linked to an object container": write title: {text: "..."} instead of a plain string.
- "frames" is reported as an unsupported key: animations are not available; use layout.sliders or updatemenus.
- After inserting, ask the user to confirm the block renders as a chart in reading view, or use read_charts to confirm it is found with no problems.
